title: FoundationDB Profile Analyzer
description: Transaction profiles tailed from FoundationDB. The query analyzer ranks prefixes by cost; the hotspot tables show the per-key skew that prefix-level aggregates hide.

list.name: datasource
list.label: Data source
list.description: Which ClickHouse this dashboard reads. Every panel and variable follows it.

list.name: cluster
list.label: Cluster
list.description: Which FoundationDB cluster's data to look at. In production several clusters feed one ClickHouse; every row carries the label its agent was configured with (fdb.cluster_name).
list.definition: SELECT DISTINCT cluster FROM fdb_profiles.operations ORDER BY cluster
list.query: SELECT DISTINCT cluster FROM fdb_profiles.operations ORDER BY cluster

list.name: key_prefix
list.label: Key prefix
list.description: Configured prefixes from config.yaml, first-16-bytes (unknown) labels for unmatched keys, plus (other) and (system).
list.definition: SELECT DISTINCT key_prefix FROM fdb_profiles.operations WHERE key_prefix != '' AND (cluster IN ($cluster) OR '__all__' IN ($cluster)) ORDER BY key_prefix
list.query: SELECT DISTINCT key_prefix FROM fdb_profiles.operations WHERE key_prefix != '' AND (cluster IN ($cluster) OR '__all__' IN ($cluster)) ORDER BY key_prefix

list.name: op_type
list.label: Operation
list.definition: SELECT DISTINCT op_type FROM fdb_profiles.operations WHERE op_type != '' AND (cluster IN ($cluster) OR '__all__' IN ($cluster)) ORDER BY op_type
list.query: SELECT DISTINCT op_type FROM fdb_profiles.operations WHERE op_type != '' AND (cluster IN ($cluster) OR '__all__' IN ($cluster)) ORDER BY op_type

list.name: dc_id
list.label: Data centre
list.definition: SELECT DISTINCT dc_id FROM fdb_profiles.operations WHERE dc_id != '' AND (cluster IN ($cluster) OR '__all__' IN ($cluster)) ORDER BY dc_id
list.query: SELECT DISTINCT dc_id FROM fdb_profiles.operations WHERE dc_id != '' AND (cluster IN ($cluster) OR '__all__' IN ($cluster)) ORDER BY dc_id

list.name: percentile
list.label: Latency percentile
list.description: Which latency quantile the latency panel draws.

list.name: range_depth
list.label: Range depth (bytes)
list.description: How many leading key bytes define a range bucket in Hot key ranges.

panels.title: Client sample rate
panels.description:
The fraction of transactions FoundationDB samples, as `fdbcli> profile client set <rate> <size>` last left it. This is the volume control on every count elsewhere on this dashboard: at 0.01 each row below stands for about a hundred transactions.

Stepped, because it holds until an operator changes it. Deliberately not filtered by the variables above — it is cluster-wide, and the point of having it here is to see it whatever else is selected. A gap means no ingester was running, which is not the same as profiling being off; that reads as zero.

To study only finely sampled data, drag-select a raised-rate window here: it sets the dashboard time range.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  $__timeInterval(sampled_at) AS time,
  max(sample_rate)            AS "Sample rate"
FROM fdb_profiles.profiling_config
WHERE $__timeFilter(sampled_at)
  AND (cluster IN ($cluster) OR '__all__' IN ($cluster))
GROUP BY time
ORDER BY time

panels.title: Profile buffer
panels.description:
How much of the profile keyspace's size cap is in use, against the cap itself — the `<size>` half of `profile client set`.

Used approaching Limit is the warning sign: FoundationDB then trims the ring buffer oldest-first, past a lagging ingester's cursor if it has fallen behind. That is the one failure mode in this pipeline that loses profile records silently, with no error anywhere.

When the buffer laps a slow or stopped ingester, the loss is not silent: a red history-gap annotation appears across every panel, and the History loss stat counts it.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  $__timeInterval(sampled_at)                     AS time,
  maxIf(ring_buffer_bytes, ring_buffer_valid = 1) AS "Used",
  max(size_limit)                                 AS "Limit",
  maxIf(ring_buffer_bytes, ring_buffer_valid = 1)
    / greatest(max(size_limit), 1)                AS "Used %"
FROM fdb_profiles.profiling_config
WHERE $__timeFilter(sampled_at)
  AND (cluster IN ($cluster) OR '__all__' IN ($cluster))
GROUP BY time
ORDER BY time

panels.title: History loss
panels.description:
What the ring buffer has torn out of the recorded history in the selected window.

Gaps counts loss EVENTS — occasions when the buffer's trim horizon passed an ingester's cursor, live or across a restart. A gap's size in records is unknowable (the records are gone), so it is deliberately not shown as a record count: that number would be an invention. Dropped records is the countable structural loss — records whose remaining chunks were trimmed or evicted mid-reassembly.

Anything non-zero here means charts below under-report for part of this window. Losing history is an accepted trade — the pipeline never pushes back on the cluster — but it is only acceptable because this panel and the red annotations make it visible.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT sum(laps + resume_gaps) AS "Gaps",
       sum(records_dropped)    AS "Dropped records"
FROM fdb_profiles.profiling_config
WHERE $__timeFilter(sampled_at)
  AND (cluster IN ($cluster) OR '__all__' IN ($cluster))

SELECT count() AS ops
FROM fdb_profiles.operations
WHERE $__timeFilter(event_time)
  AND (cluster IN ($cluster) OR '__all__' IN ($cluster))
  AND (key_prefix IN ($key_prefix) OR '__all__' IN ($key_prefix))
  AND (op_type IN ($op_type) OR '__all__' IN ($op_type))
  AND (dc_id IN ($dc_id) OR '__all__' IN ($dc_id))

SELECT count() / greatest(toUnixTimestamp($__toTime) - toUnixTimestamp($__fromTime), 1) AS ops_per_sec
FROM fdb_profiles.operations
WHERE $__timeFilter(event_time)
  AND (cluster IN ($cluster) OR '__all__' IN ($cluster))
  AND (key_prefix IN ($key_prefix) OR '__all__' IN ($key_prefix))
  AND (op_type IN ($op_type) OR '__all__' IN ($op_type))
  AND (dc_id IN ($dc_id) OR '__all__' IN ($dc_id))

SELECT countIf(error_code != 0) * 100.0 / greatest(count(), 1) AS error_pct
FROM fdb_profiles.operations
WHERE $__timeFilter(event_time)
  AND (cluster IN ($cluster) OR '__all__' IN ($cluster))
  AND (key_prefix IN ($key_prefix) OR '__all__' IN ($key_prefix))
  AND (op_type IN ($op_type) OR '__all__' IN ($op_type))
  AND (dc_id IN ($dc_id) OR '__all__' IN ($dc_id))

SELECT quantile(0.99)(latency) AS p99
FROM fdb_profiles.operations
WHERE $__timeFilter(event_time) AND latency > 0
  AND (cluster IN ($cluster) OR '__all__' IN ($cluster))
  AND (key_prefix IN ($key_prefix) OR '__all__' IN ($key_prefix))
  AND (op_type IN ($op_type) OR '__all__' IN ($op_type))
  AND (dc_id IN ($dc_id) OR '__all__' IN ($dc_id))

panels.title: Operations by prefix
panels.description: Load is total time divided by the wall-clock length of the selected range: the average number of operations in flight, and therefore how much of the cluster this prefix is occupying. It ranks by real cost rather than raw frequency, which is why it is the default sort. Every column header is sortable.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  key_prefix                                    AS "Prefix",
  op_type                                       AS "Op",
  sparkbar(20, toUnixTimestamp($__fromTime), toUnixTimestamp($__toTime))(toUnixTimestamp(event_time), 1)                                       AS "Activity",
  sum(latency) / greatest(toUnixTimestamp($__toTime) - toUnixTimestamp($__fromTime), 1)                      AS "Load",
  count()                                       AS "Count",
  round(sum(if(sample_rate > 0, 1.0 / sample_rate, 1.0))) AS "Est. count",
  count() / greatest(toUnixTimestamp($__toTime) - toUnixTimestamp($__fromTime), 1)                           AS "Ops/sec",
  sum(latency)                                  AS "Total time",
  avg(latency)                                  AS "Avg",
  quantile(0.95)(latency)                       AS "p95",
  quantile(0.99)(latency)                       AS "p99",
  max(latency)                                  AS "Max",
  countIf(error_code != 0)                      AS "Errors"
FROM fdb_profiles.operations
WHERE $__timeFilter(event_time)
  AND (cluster IN ($cluster) OR '__all__' IN ($cluster))
  AND (key_prefix IN ($key_prefix) OR '__all__' IN ($key_prefix))
  AND (op_type IN ($op_type) OR '__all__' IN ($op_type))
  AND (dc_id IN ($dc_id) OR '__all__' IN ($dc_id))
GROUP BY key_prefix, op_type
ORDER BY "Load" DESC

panels.title: Throughput by operation
panels.description: One series per operation type, decoded from the profile record. A flat zero error_* trio is the healthy state.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  $__timeInterval(event_time) AS time,
  countIf(op_type = 'get')             AS get,
  countIf(op_type = 'get_range')       AS get_range,
  countIf(op_type = 'get_version')     AS get_version,
  countIf(op_type = 'commit')          AS commit,
  countIf(op_type = 'error_get')       AS error_get,
  countIf(op_type = 'error_get_range') AS error_get_range,
  countIf(op_type = 'error_commit')    AS error_commit
FROM fdb_profiles.operations
WHERE $__timeFilter(event_time)
  AND (cluster IN ($cluster) OR '__all__' IN ($cluster))
  AND (key_prefix IN ($key_prefix) OR '__all__' IN ($key_prefix))
  AND (op_type IN ($op_type) OR '__all__' IN ($op_type))
  AND (dc_id IN ($dc_id) OR '__all__' IN ($dc_id))
GROUP BY time
ORDER BY time

panels.title: ${percentile:text} latency by operation
panels.description: The selected percentile (picker at the top, default p99) per operation type. Error events carry no latency and are excluded.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  $__timeInterval(event_time) AS time,
  quantileIf($percentile)(latency, op_type = 'get')         AS get,
  quantileIf($percentile)(latency, op_type = 'get_range')   AS get_range,
  quantileIf($percentile)(latency, op_type = 'get_version') AS get_version,
  quantileIf($percentile)(latency, op_type = 'commit')      AS commit
FROM fdb_profiles.operations
WHERE $__timeFilter(event_time) AND latency > 0
  AND (cluster IN ($cluster) OR '__all__' IN ($cluster))
  AND (key_prefix IN ($key_prefix) OR '__all__' IN ($key_prefix))
  AND (op_type IN ($op_type) OR '__all__' IN ($op_type))
  AND (dc_id IN ($dc_id) OR '__all__' IN ($dc_id))
GROUP BY time
ORDER BY time

panels.title: Hot read keys
panels.description: Cumulative share is the point of this table: 'the top 10 keys are 60% of all reads' is a finding, and a flat distribution is equally a finding.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  key                                                             AS "Key",
  if(key = '', '(empty)', hex(key))                                                        AS "hex(key)",
  sparkbar(20, toUnixTimestamp($__fromTime), toUnixTimestamp($__toTime))(toUnixTimestamp(event_time), 1)                                                         AS "Activity",
  count()                                                         AS "Reads",
  round(sum(if(sample_rate > 0, 1.0 / sample_rate, 1.0))) AS "Est. reads",
  count() * 100.0 / sum(count()) OVER ()                          AS "Share",
  sum(count()) OVER (ORDER BY count() DESC, key
                     ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW)
    * 100.0 / sum(count()) OVER ()                                AS "Cumulative",
  avg(latency)                                                    AS "Avg latency",
  sum(value_size)                                                 AS "Bytes read"
FROM fdb_profiles.operations
WHERE $__timeFilter(event_time)
  AND (cluster IN ($cluster) OR '__all__' IN ($cluster))
  AND op_type = 'get'
  AND (key_prefix IN ($key_prefix) OR '__all__' IN ($key_prefix))
  AND (dc_id IN ($dc_id) OR '__all__' IN ($dc_id))
GROUP BY key
ORDER BY "Reads" DESC, "Key"
LIMIT 50

panels.title: Hot write keys
panels.description: Counts SET_VALUE and ADD_VALUE mutations, the same pair FoundationDB's own analyzer uses. Cumulative share is the point of this table: 'the top 10 keys are 60% of all reads' is a finding, and a flat distribution is equally a finding.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  key                                                             AS "Key",
  if(key = '', '(empty)', hex(key))                                                        AS "hex(key)",
  sparkbar(20, toUnixTimestamp($__fromTime), toUnixTimestamp($__toTime))(toUnixTimestamp(event_time), 1)                                                         AS "Activity",
  count()                                                         AS "Writes",
  round(sum(if(sample_rate > 0, 1.0 / sample_rate, 1.0))) AS "Est. writes",
  count() * 100.0 / sum(count()) OVER ()                          AS "Share",
  sum(count()) OVER (ORDER BY count() DESC, key
                     ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW)
    * 100.0 / sum(count()) OVER ()                                AS "Cumulative",
  sum(value_size)                                                 AS "Bytes written"
FROM fdb_profiles.mutations
WHERE $__timeFilter(event_time)
  AND (cluster IN ($cluster) OR '__all__' IN ($cluster))
  AND mutation_type IN ('SET_VALUE', 'ADD_VALUE')
  AND (key_prefix IN ($key_prefix) OR '__all__' IN ($key_prefix))
GROUP BY key
ORDER BY "Writes" DESC, "Key"
LIMIT 50

panels.title: Hot scanned ranges
panels.description: Literal get_range calls, grouped by their exact (begin, end) pair: WHICH SCANS run hot. A single wide scan can outweigh thousands of point reads. Contrast with Hot keyspace regions, which ignores call shapes and asks where in the keyspace traffic lands.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  key                                                             AS "Begin",
  if(key = '', '(empty)', hex(key))                                                        AS "hex(key)",
  end_key                                                         AS "End",
  if(end_key = '', '(empty)', hex(end_key))                                                    AS "hex(end_key)",
  sparkbar(20, toUnixTimestamp($__fromTime), toUnixTimestamp($__toTime))(toUnixTimestamp(event_time), 1)                                                         AS "Activity",
  count()                                                         AS "Scans",
  round(sum(if(sample_rate > 0, 1.0 / sample_rate, 1.0))) AS "Est. scans",
  count() * 100.0 / sum(count()) OVER ()                          AS "Share",
  avg(range_size)                                                 AS "Avg bytes",
  avg(latency)                                                    AS "Avg latency"
FROM fdb_profiles.operations
WHERE $__timeFilter(event_time)
  AND (cluster IN ($cluster) OR '__all__' IN ($cluster))
  AND op_type = 'get_range'
  AND (key_prefix IN ($key_prefix) OR '__all__' IN ($key_prefix))
  AND (dc_id IN ($dc_id) OR '__all__' IN ($dc_id))
GROUP BY key, end_key
ORDER BY "Scans" DESC, "Begin"
LIMIT 25

panels.title: Hot keyspace regions
panels.description: Every read and written key, bucketed by its first $range_depth bytes and ranked by combined traffic: WHERE in the keyspace load lands, regardless of whether it arrived as gets, scans or writes. 'Distinct keys' separates one hot key (low) from a genuinely hot region (high). Adjust the depth variable to zoom the bucketing in or out.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  substring(key, 1, $range_depth)                                 AS "Range",
  if(substring(key, 1, $range_depth) = '', '(empty)', hex(substring(key, 1, $range_depth)))                            AS "hex(range)",
  sparkbar(20, toUnixTimestamp($__fromTime), toUnixTimestamp($__toTime))(toUnixTimestamp(event_time), 1)                                                         AS "Activity",
  count()                                                         AS "Ops",
  round(sum(if(sample_rate > 0, 1.0 / sample_rate, 1.0))) AS "Est. ops",
  countIf(kind = 'read')                                          AS "Reads",
  countIf(kind = 'write')                                         AS "Writes",
  uniqExact(key)                                                  AS "Distinct keys",
  count() * 100.0 / sum(count()) OVER ()                          AS "Share",
  sum(count()) OVER (ORDER BY count() DESC, substring(key, 1, $range_depth)
                     ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW)
    * 100.0 / sum(count()) OVER ()                                AS "Cumulative"
FROM (
    SELECT key, cluster, key_prefix, event_time, sample_rate, 'read' AS kind
    FROM fdb_profiles.operations
    WHERE op_type IN ('get', 'get_range') AND key != ''
    UNION ALL
    SELECT key, cluster, key_prefix, event_time, sample_rate, 'write' AS kind
    FROM fdb_profiles.mutations
    WHERE mutation_type IN ('SET_VALUE', 'ADD_VALUE')
)
WHERE $__timeFilter(event_time)
  AND (cluster IN ($cluster) OR '__all__' IN ($cluster))
  AND (key_prefix IN ($key_prefix) OR '__all__' IN ($key_prefix))
GROUP BY "Range"
ORDER BY "Ops" DESC, "Range"
LIMIT 40

panels.title: Commits and conflicts
panels.description: Commits against commits that lost a conflict (error 1020, decoded as error_commit). A rising conflicts share means transactions are racing over the same keys — the table beside this names the ranges.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  $__timeInterval(event_time)          AS time,
  countIf(op_type = 'commit')          AS commits,
  countIf(op_type = 'error_commit')    AS conflicts
FROM fdb_profiles.operations
WHERE $__timeFilter(event_time)
  AND (cluster IN ($cluster) OR '__all__' IN ($cluster))
  AND op_type IN ('commit', 'error_commit')
  AND (key_prefix IN ($key_prefix) OR '__all__' IN ($key_prefix))
  AND (dc_id IN ($dc_id) OR '__all__' IN ($dc_id))
GROUP BY time
ORDER BY time

panels.title: Conflicting ranges
panels.description: The read and write conflict ranges carried by transactions that lost a conflict, ranked by how often each range was involved. `read` rows are what the loser had read — the data a winner invalidated under it; `write` rows are what it was trying to write. A range topping this table is the contention point to redesign around. Answers the question the conflict_ranges table was recorded for.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  begin_key                                               AS "Begin",
  if(begin_key = '', '(empty)', hex(begin_key))                                          AS "hex(begin_key)",
  end_key                                                 AS "End",
  if(end_key = '', '(empty)', hex(end_key))                                            AS "hex(end_key)",
  kind                                                    AS "Kind",
  sparkbar(20, toUnixTimestamp($__fromTime), toUnixTimestamp($__toTime))(toUnixTimestamp(event_time), 1) AS "Activity",
  count()                                                 AS "Conflicts",
  round(sum(if(sample_rate > 0, 1.0 / sample_rate, 1.0))) AS "Est. conflicts",
  uniqExact(transaction_id)                               AS "Failed txns",
  count() * 100.0 / sum(count()) OVER ()                  AS "Share"
FROM fdb_profiles.conflict_ranges
WHERE $__timeFilter(event_time)
  AND (cluster IN ($cluster) OR '__all__' IN ($cluster))
  AND (key_prefix IN ($key_prefix) OR '__all__' IN ($key_prefix))
  AND transaction_id GLOBAL IN (
    SELECT transaction_id FROM fdb_profiles.operations
    WHERE $__timeFilter(event_time) AND op_type = 'error_commit'
      AND (cluster IN ($cluster) OR '__all__' IN ($cluster))
  )
GROUP BY begin_key, end_key, kind
ORDER BY "Conflicts" DESC, "Begin"
LIMIT 25

panels.title: Recent operations
panels.description: The raw operations behind the aggregates — the drill-down target of the prefix links in the query analyzer. Filtered by the same variables as everything else.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  event_time                        AS "Time",
  key_prefix                        AS "Prefix",
  op_type                           AS "Op",
  key                               AS "Key",
  if(key = '', '(empty)', hex(key))                          AS "hex(key)",
  latency                           AS "Latency",
  value_size                        AS "Value bytes",
  range_size                        AS "Range bytes",
  num_mutations                     AS "Mutations",
  commit_bytes                      AS "Commit bytes",
  error_code                        AS "Error",
  transaction_id                    AS "Txn"
FROM fdb_profiles.operations
WHERE $__timeFilter(event_time)
  AND (cluster IN ($cluster) OR '__all__' IN ($cluster))
  AND (key_prefix IN ($key_prefix) OR '__all__' IN ($key_prefix))
  AND (op_type IN ($op_type) OR '__all__' IN ($op_type))
  AND (dc_id IN ($dc_id) OR '__all__' IN ($dc_id))
ORDER BY event_time DESC
LIMIT 200

target.rawSql:
SELECT toUnixTimestamp64Milli(sampled_at) AS time,
       multiIf(laps > 0 AND resume_gaps > 0, 'Profile history gap: ring buffer lapped, live and across a restart',
               laps > 0, 'Profile history gap: ring buffer lapped the running ingester; records were trimmed unread',
               'Profile history gap across an ingester restart: records written meanwhile may have been trimmed unread') AS text,
       'history-gap' AS tags
FROM fdb_profiles.profiling_config
WHERE $__timeFilter(sampled_at) AND (laps > 0 OR resume_gaps > 0)
  AND (cluster IN ($cluster) OR '__all__' IN ($cluster))
ORDER BY time
